subject: Geography
sub_topic: Lakes of India — freshwater and saltwater

concepts.name: Classification of Indian Lakes: Origin and Formation Types
key_dimensions: Tectonic lakes (Wular, Kolleru) vs. glacial lakes (Dal, Tsomoriri) vs. lagoon lakes (Chilika, Pulicat) — formation mechanisms
Oxbow/fluvial lakes formed by river meandering (Kanwar, Kabar) — distinction from reservoirs
Aeolian (wind-formed) lakes in Rajasthan (Sambhar, Didwana) — role of wind-deflation basins
UPSC trap: Distinguishing natural lakes from man-made reservoirs that are often confused as natural (e.g., Gobind Sagar vs. Dal Lake)

concepts.name: Chilika Lake: Ecology, Hydrology, and Conservation Status
key_dimensions: Largest coastal lagoon in India and Asia's largest brackish water lagoon — seasonal salinity variation mechanism
Ramsar Site designation (1981) — first Indian wetland on Ramsar list; also under National Wetland Conservation Programme
Irrawaddy dolphins, migratory birds (bar-headed geese), and fisheries economy — ecological significance
UPSC trap: Chilika is brackish (not purely saltwater or freshwater) — salinity changes with seasons and the inlet channel location controversy

concepts.name: Wular Lake: Formation, Significance, and Geopolitical Context
key_dimensions: Largest freshwater lake in India (J&K) — tectonic origin in Kashmir Valley linked to Jhelum River dynamics
Distinction from Dal Lake: Wular is natural + tectonic; Dal is glacial-fed + heavily modified by human activity
Tulbul Navigation Project (Wullar Barrage) — India-Pakistan dispute under Indus Waters Treaty context
UPSC trap: Often confused with Dal Lake as 'largest in J&K' — Wular is largest by area; Dal is most famous

concepts.name: Sambhar Lake: Salinity Mechanism and Economic Importance
key_dimensions: Largest inland saltwater lake in India — located in Rajasthan; mechanism of salinity (landlocked basin, high evaporation, no outflow)
Source of salt production — supplies ~8% of India's salt; designated Ramsar site for migratory flamingos
Hydrological uniqueness: fed by rivers Mendha, Rupangarh, Khari — yet remains saline due to endorheic drainage
UPSC trap: Comparing Sambhar (inland saltwater) with Chilika (coastal brackish) — different salinity mechanisms entirely

concepts.name: Loktak Lake: Phumdis and Conservation Conflicts
key_dimensions: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India — located in Manipur; only floating national park (Keibul Lamjao) in the world
Phumdis: heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter — unique ecological feature; habitat of Sangai deer (brow-antlered deer)
Ramsar site (1990) — also listed under Montreux Record due to ecological degradation from Loktak Hydroelectric Project
UPSC trap: Keibul Lamjao is a national park ON the lake (floating) — not an island park; Sangai is State animal of Manipur

concepts.name: Dal Lake: Characteristics, Threats, and Urban Pressures
key_dimensions: Glacially-fed urban lake in Srinagar — fed by springs and precipitation; connected to Nagin Lake
Shrinkage due to encroachment, eutrophication from houseboat waste, and siltation — flagship urban lake degradation case
Floating gardens (Rad) and floating markets — socio-economic cultural significance
UPSC trap: Dal is NOT the largest lake in J&K (Wular is); Dal is glacial-fed but not a glacial lake in the strict landform sense

concepts.name: Tsomoriri and High-Altitude Lakes of Ladakh
key_dimensions: Tsomoriri: highest Ramsar-designated wetland in the world (~4,522 m) — in Ladakh; saltwater lake of tectonic-glacial origin
Pangong Tso: transboundary lake (India-China) — 60% in China; brackish water; unique blue-green colour due to mineral content
Tso Kar: saltwater lake used for borax extraction — part of Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary
UPSC trap: Pangong Tso is brackish NOT freshwater despite popular perception; Tsomoriri is Ramsar site but Pangong is NOT

concepts.name: Pulicat Lake: Second Largest Saltwater Lagoon and State Boundary Issue
key_dimensions: Second largest coastal lagoon/brackish lake in India after Chilika — located on Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border
Sriharikota Island separates it from the Bay of Bengal — ISRO launch station is on this barrier island
Flamingo Festival and migratory bird habitat — pelicans, flamingos
UPSC trap: Pulicat straddles two states (AP and TN) — most of the lake is in AP; often wrongly placed entirely in TN

concepts.name: Kolleru Lake: Tectonic Origin and Ramsar Designation
key_dimensions: Largest freshwater lake in India located between Krishna and Godavari deltas (Andhra Pradesh) — tectonic depression
Designated as Ramsar site and Wildlife Sanctuary — habitat for painted storks, pelicans
Ecological degradation due to aquaculture (prawn/fish farming) encroachment — Supreme Court intervention
UPSC trap: Kolleru is often confused with Pulicat (also in AP) — Kolleru is freshwater + tectonic; Pulicat is brackish + lagoon

concepts.name: Freshwater vs. Saltwater Lakes: Determining Factors
key_dimensions: Key determinant: drainage type — exorheic (outflow → freshwater) vs. endorheic (no outflow → salt accumulates)
Role of evaporation rate, catchment geology, and proximity to sea in determining salinity levels
Indian examples mapped to type: Wular/Kolleru (freshwater-exorheic) vs. Sambhar/Tso Kar (saltwater-endorheic) vs. Chilika/Pulicat (brackish-coastal)
UPSC trap: Not all coastal lakes are saltwater (Kolleru is freshwater though near coast); not all inland lakes are freshwater (Sambhar is inland but saline)

concepts.name: Lagoon Lakes of India: Formation and Coastal Geomorphology
key_dimensions: Formation process: longshore drift creating barrier spits/bars that enclose a water body — distinguishing lagoons from other lake types
Major lagoons: Chilika (Odisha), Pulicat (AP/TN), Ashtamudi (Kerala), Vembanad (Kerala) — distribution along east vs. west coast
East coast has more lagoons than west coast — reason: gentle slope, sediment-rich rivers, stronger longshore drift on east coast
UPSC trap: Vembanad is often called a lake but is technically an estuary-lagoon; Ashtamudi is a Ramsar site; both are Kerala backwaters

concepts.name: Ramsar Sites Among Indian Lakes: Coverage and Criteria
key_dimensions: Ramsar Convention criteria for wetland designation — India's Ramsar sites list (75+ as of 2023) — lakes that qualify
Key Ramsar lakes: Chilika (1981, first), Loktak (1990), Sambhar, Tsomoriri, Kolleru, Ashtamudi, Vembanad, Pulicat
Montreux Record: Chilika and Loktak listed due to ecological degradation — significance of this 'watch list'
UPSC trap: Chilika was REMOVED from Montreux Record in 2002 after restoration; Loktak REMAINS on it — frequently reversed in questions

concepts.name: Oxbow Lakes in India: Formation and Floodplain Ecology
key_dimensions: Formation: river meanders cut off to form crescent-shaped lakes — most common in Ganga-Brahmaputra floodplains
Bihar's ox-bow lakes: Kanwar Lake (Begusarai) — Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake; Kabar Taal — Ramsar site
Ecological role: fish breeding, bird habitat, groundwater recharge in floodplain systems
UPSC trap: Kanwar/Kabar are often confused — Kanwar Taal (also called Kawar) is Ramsar-designated; distinction from reservoirs

concepts.name: Vembanad Lake: Kerala's Largest Lake and Backwater System
key_dimensions: Longest lake in India (~96 km) and largest in Kerala — Ramsar site; part of the Kerala backwater system
Thanneermukkam Bund: divides Vembanad into saline (west) and freshwater (east) zones — impact on ecology and fisheries
Nehru Trophy Boat Race conducted on Punnamada Lake — which is a portion of Vembanad
UPSC trap: Punnamada Lake is NOT a separate lake — it is a part of Vembanad; Vembanad is brackish, not purely freshwater

concepts.name: Glacial Lakes and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) in India
key_dimensions: Glacial lakes formed by moraine damming or ice damming in Himalayan regions — Sikkim, Uttarakhand, HP, J&K
GLOF mechanism: rapid drainage when moraine/ice dam fails — Sikkim GLOF (October 2023) destroying Teesta dams — recent case study
South Lhonak Lake (Sikkim), Shako Cho — inventory by ISRO/GSI; climate change accelerating glacial lake expansion
UPSC trap: GLOFs are distinct from cloudbursts and flash floods — specific to glacially dammed lakes; Himalayan states most vulnerable

concepts.name: Lonar Lake: Meteorite Impact Crater Lake
key_dimensions: Only known hyper-velocity meteorite impact crater lake in basaltic rock — located in Buldhana district, Maharashtra
Unique chemistry: simultaneously saline AND alkaline — hosts extremophile microorganisms; recent discovery of turning pink (2020)
Designated as Ramsar site (2020) and National Geo-heritage Monument — dual protected status
UPSC trap: Lonar is saline due to volcanic basalt mineral leaching + endorheic drainage, NOT due to marine origin — origin is meteoric impact, not tectonic/volcanic

concepts.name: Saline Lakes of Rajasthan: Distribution and Economic Use
key_dimensions: Cluster of saline lakes in Rajasthan: Sambhar, Didwana, Pachpadra, Lunkaransar — all endorheic basins in Aravalli rain shadow zone
Salt extraction economy — Sambhar Lake owned by Sambhar Salts Ltd (joint venture of GoI and Rajasthan govt)
Palaeoclimatic significance: ancient seabed theory vs. aeolian concentration theory for salinity origin
UPSC trap: Not all Rajasthan lakes are saline — Pichola, Fateh Sagar (Udaipur) are freshwater; only endorheic desert lakes are saline

concepts.name: Lakes and River Connectivity: Floodplain Lake Dynamics
key_dimensions: Seasonal connectivity between rivers and adjacent lakes during floods — Wular connected to Jhelum; Kolleru connected to Krishna-Godavari
Role of lakes as natural flood buffers — Wular absorbs Jhelum floods; Dal Lake's role in Kashmir flood management (2014 floods)
Groundwater-lake interaction: lakes recharging aquifers vs. aquifers feeding lakes — springs feeding Dal Lake example
UPSC trap: Lakes connected to rivers are NOT classified as reservoirs; natural flood-plain lakes serve different ecological and hydrological functions than dams

concepts.name: Urban Lake Degradation and Conservation Initiatives
key_dimensions: Major threats: encroachment, eutrophication (excess nutrients from sewage/agriculture), siltation, invasive species (water hyacinth)
National Lake Conservation Plan (NLCP) — nodal ministry (MoEFCC), target lakes, funding pattern
Benchmark cases: Dal (J&K), Hussain Sagar (Hyderabad — industrial pollution + idol immersion), Powai (Mumbai)
UPSC trap: NLCP vs. National Wetland Conservation Programme (NWCP) — different schemes with different scope; lakes may be covered under either or both

concepts.name: Sundarbans and Coastal Wetland Lakes vs. Inland Lakes: Distinction
key_dimensions: Distinction between tidal wetlands/estuarine lakes and true inland lakes — importance for UPSC classification questions
Chilika, Pulicat, Vembanad as coastal lagoon-type lakes — tidal influence, salinity gradient, mangrove association
Inland freshwater lakes (Wular, Loktak, Kolleru) — no tidal influence, different biodiversity and conservation frameworks
UPSC trap: Mangrove-associated water bodies in Sundarbans/Andamans are NOT classified as lakes — they are tidal creeks/estuaries; important for exclusion-based questions
